sets.relationshipLabel: category and a kind of it
sets.explanation: Cotton candy is a kind of snack and a roller coaster is a kind of ride — each pair names a category and one example inside it.

sets.relationshipLabel: a faltering form falling short of the full version
sets.explanation: A sputter is a hum that never fully catches, and a flicker is a glow that never fully steadies — each first word is the failed attempt at the second.

sets.relationshipLabel: the rule or danger that forces a stop before the thing can happen
sets.explanation: A curfew cuts off an encore and a washout cuts off a parade — each first word is the reason the second word never gets to happen, and the two causes differ sharply in kind so they can't be swapped.

sets.relationshipLabel: worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A roustabout swings a mallet and a rigger turns a wrench — each worker is defined by the tool that does their job.

glossary.definition: a laborer who does general physical work, often setting up or tearing down at a traveling show
